69762-hellflower.title: Hellflower
69762-hellflower.creator: Unknown
69762-hellflower.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Farradyne laughed shortly, but the sound was all scorn and no humor. While his raw bark was still echoing in the room, Farradyne added, "Drop it, Clevis. With a thousand licensed spacemen handy everywhere, willing to latch onto an honest buck, any man that comes half way across Venus to offer Farradyne a job can't be on the level."

arxiv-2011-07891.title: Surface corrugated laminates as elastic grating couplers: splitting of SV- and P-waves by selective diffraction
arxiv-2011-07891.creator: G. J. Chaplain, R. V. Craster
arxiv-2011-07891.description: Abstract The phenomenon of selective diffraction is extended to in-plane elastic waves and we design surface corrugated periodic laminates that incorporate crystal momentum transfer which, due to the rich physics embedded within the vector elastic system, results in frequency, angle and wave-type selective diffraction.

arxiv-2205-08442.title: Flatness of the nuclear norm sphere, simultaneous polarization, and uniqueness in nuclear norm minimization Thanks: The first and second author are partially supported by an NSERC discovery grant
arxiv-2205-08442.creator: Tim Hoheisel, Elliot Paquette
arxiv-2205-08442.description: Abstract . In this paper we establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of line segments (or flats ) in the sphere of the nuclear norm via the notion of simultaneous polarization and a refined expression for the subdifferential of the nuclear norm.

arxiv-2303-18105.title: The novel XYU-GEM to resolve ambiguities
arxiv-2303-18105.creator: R. Veenhof
arxiv-2303-18105.description: Abstract Removing ambiguities within a single stage becomes crucial when one can not use multiple detectors behind each other to resolve them which naturally is the case for neutral radiation. An example would be RICH detectors. Commonly pixilated readout is choosen for this purpose. However, this causes a remarkable increase in quantity of channels and does not scale up well.

arxiv-2304-14832.title: Comparison of SAT-Based and ASP-Based Algorithms for Inconsistency Measurement
arxiv-2304-14832.creator: Isabelle Kuhlmann isabelle.kuhlmann@fernuni-hagen.de, Anna Gessler anna.gessler.work@gmail.com, Vivien Laszlo vivien.laszlo@fernuni-hagen.de
arxiv-2304-14832.description: Abstract We present algorithms based on satisfiability problem (SAT) solving, as well as answer set programming (ASP), for solving the problem of determining inconsistency degrees in propositional knowledge bases. We consider six different inconsistency measures whose respective decision problems lie on the first level of the polynomial hierarchy.

arxiv-2308-02031.title: Knowledge-enhanced Neuro-Symbolic AI for Cybersecurity and Privacy
arxiv-2308-02031.creator: Aritran Piplai 1 , Anantaa Kotal 1 , Seyedreza Mohseni 1 , Manas Gaur 1 , Sudip Mittal 2 , and Anupam Joshi 1
arxiv-2308-02031.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Aritran Piplai 1 , Anantaa Kotal 1 , Seyedreza Mohseni 1 , Manas Gaur 1 , Sudip Mittal 2 , and Anupam Joshi 1. Neuro-Symbolic Artificial Intelligence (AI) is an emerging and quickly advancing field that combines the subsymbolic strengths of (deep) neural networks and explicit, symbolic knowledge contained in knowledge graphs to enhance explainability and safety in AI systems.

arxiv-2503-02737.title: Large Language Models for Multilingual Previously Fact-Checked Claim Detection
arxiv-2503-02737.creator: Ivan Vykopal, Matúš Pikuliak, Simon Ostermann, Tatiana Anikina, Michal Gregor, Marián Šimko
arxiv-2503-02737.description: Abstract In our era of widespread false information, human fact-checkers often face the challenge of duplicating efforts when verifying claims that may have already been addressed in other countries or languages. As false information transcends linguistic boundaries, the ability to automatically detect previously fact-checked claims across languages has become an increasingly important task.

arxiv-2504-07179.title: Prospects for detecting new dark physics with the next generation of atomic clocks
arxiv-2504-07179.creator: Benjamin Elder, Giorgio Mentasti, Elizabeth Pasatembou, Charles F. A. Baynham, Oliver Buchmueller, Carlo R. Contaldi, Claudia de Rham, Richard Hobson, Andrew J. Tolley
arxiv-2504-07179.description: Abstract Wide classes of new fundamental physics theories cause apparent variations in particle mass ratios in space and time. In theories that violate the weak equivalence principle (EP), those variations are not uniform across all particles and may be detected with atomic and molecular clock frequency comparisons.

arxiv-2504-21513.title: Internal solitary and cnoidal waves of moderate amplitude in a two-layer fluid: the extended KdV equation approximation
arxiv-2504-21513.creator: Nerijus Sidorovas a , Dmitri Tseluiko a , Wooyoung Choi b , Karima Khusnutdinova a,∗
arxiv-2504-21513.description: Abstract We consider travelling internal waves in a two-layer fluid with linear shear currents from the viewpoint of the extended Korteweg-de Vries (eKdV) equation derived from a strongly-nonlinear long-wave model. Using an asymptotic Kodama-Fokas-Liu near-identity transformation, we map the eKdV equation to the Gardner equation.

arxiv-2506-01067.title: Typical T T -free graphs
arxiv-2506-01067.creator: Bruce Reed, Yelena Yuditsky
arxiv-2506-01067.description: Abstract We prove that for every tree T T which is not an edge, for almost every graph G G which does not contain T T as an induced subgraph, V ⁡ ( G ) V(G) has a partition into α ⁡ ( T ) − 1 \alpha(T)-1 parts certifying this fact.

arxiv-2508-04215.title: Robust estimation of causal dose-response relationship using exposure data with dose as an instrumental variable
arxiv-2508-04215.creator: Jixian Wang, Zhiwei Zhang, Ram Tiwari
arxiv-2508-04215.description: Abstract An accurate estimation of the dose-response relationship is important to determine the optimal dose. For this purpose, a dose finding trial in which subjects are randomized to a few fixed dose levels is the most commonly used design. Often, the estimation uses response data only, although drug exposure data are often obtained during the trial.

arxiv-2511-07821.title: SynTTS-Commands: A Public Dataset for On-Device KWS via TTS-Synthesized Multilingual Speech Thanks: Citation : Lu Gan, Xi Li. SynTTS-Commands: A Public Dataset for On-Device KWS via TTS-Synthesized Multilingual Speech.
arxiv-2511-07821.creator: Lu Gan, Xi Li
arxiv-2511-07821.description: Abstract The development of high-performance, on-device keyword spotting (KWS) systems for ultra-low-power hardware is critically constrained by the scarcity of specialized, multi-command training datasets. Traditional data collection through human recording is costly, slow, and lacks scalability. This paper introduces SYNTTS-COMMANDS, a novel, multilingual voice command dataset entirely generated using state-of-the-art Text-to-Speech (TTS) synthesis.

arxiv-2512-06739.title: Non-Orthogonal Multiple-Access for Coherent-State Optical Quantum Communications Under Lossy Photon Channels Thanks: Z. Dong, X. Zhou, and X. Wang are with the Key Laboratory for Information Science of Electromagnetic Waves, School of Information Science and Technology, Fudan University, Shanghai 20
arxiv-2512-06739.creator: Zhichao Dong, Xiaolin Zhou, Yongkang Chen
arxiv-2512-06739.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Zhichao Dong, Xiaolin Zhou, Yongkang Chen. Coherent states have been increasingly considered in optical quantum communications (OQCs). With the inherent non-orthogonality of coherent states, non-orthogonal multiple-access (NOMA) naturally lends itself to the implementation of multi-user OQC. However, this remains unexplored in the literature. This paper proposes a novel successive interference cancellation (SIC)-based photon-number-resolving detection (PNRD)-Kennedy receiver for uplink NOMA-OQC systems, along with a new approach for power allocation of the coherent states emitted by users.

arxiv-2512-11797.description: Abstract The collection of large-scale and diverse robot demonstrations remains a major bottleneck for imitation learning, as real-world data acquisition is costly and simulators offer limited diversity and fidelity with pronounced sim-to-real gaps. While generative models present an attractive solution, existing methods often alter only visual appearances without creating new behaviors, or suffer from embodiment inconsistencies that yield implausible motions.

In recent years, mitophagy has received increasing attention as a research hotspot related to the...

pmc-11375580.title: Short-term outcomes after primary total mesorectal excision (TME) versus local excision followed by completion TME for early rectal cancer: population-based propensity-matched study
pmc-11375580.creator: Annabel S van Lieshout, Lisanne J H Smits, Julie M L Sijmons, Susan van Dieren, Stefan E van Oostendorp, Pieter J Tanis, Jurriaan B Tuynman
pmc-11375580.description: BackgroundColorectal cancer screening programmes have led to a shift towards early-stage colorectal cancer, which, in selected cases, can be treated using local excision. However, local excision followed by completion total mesorectal excision (two-stage approach) may be associated with less favourable outcomes than primary total mesorectal excision (one-stage approach).

pmc-11647524.title: Editorial: Neurocomputational models of language processing
pmc-11647524.creator: Markus J. Hofmann, Ya-Ning Chang, Harm Brouwer, Michael Zock
pmc-11647524.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). m to be part of natural sciences. Our objective was to bridge or at least narrow the gap between computational models, language processed by machines, and language processed by humans. While the former yield practical results, the latter provide behavioral and neural data that are invaluable for gaining insights into the strategies used by the human mind and brain to process language.

pmc-11770802.title: L’usage du tabac, de l'alcool et des drogues chez les lycéens de la ville de Gabès
pmc-11770802.creator: Hamida Kwas, Sabrine Majdoub Fehri
pmc-11770802.description: RESUMEIntroduction: Les informations sur l’usage du tabac et des autres substances illicites par les jeunes constituent un élément essentiel pour la mise en place de mesures préventives adaptées. Objectif: Déterminer la prévalence du tabagisme, de la consommation d’alcool et des drogues chez les lycéens de la ville de Gabès, Tunisie.

pmc-12417353.title: A scoping study of postpartum mental health problems and associated factors: opportunities for research and practice
pmc-12417353.creator: Oluwaseun Ojomo, Oluyemi Atibioke, Oluwapelumi Alesinloye-King, Kerstin Erlandsson, Karin Ängeby, Niklas Envall
pmc-12417353.description: ObjectiveTo provide an overview of mental health problems throughout the postpartum period and to describe the screening instruments as well as associated factors related to the relevant population.MethodsThe scoping study was guided by the framework outlined by Arksey and O’Malley and Levac et al.

pmc-12551222.title: The impact of haplotypes derived from Chinese pigs on genetic variation and economic traits in the Duroc breed
pmc-12551222.creator: Suyun Fang, Chao Guo, Hang Liu, Yuzhan Wang, Cheng Tan, Zhenfang Wu, Yiqiang Zhao, Xiaoxiang Hu, Ruifei Yang
pmc-12551222.description: BackgroundThe historical importation of Chinese pigs into Western countries has facilitated the introduction of Chinese haplotypes into European pig breeds, thereby shaping their genetic diversity and phenotypic traits. However, the genetic and biological implications of this introgression remain poorly understood.ResultsBased on SNP chip and resequencing data, we confirmed significant genetic introgression from Chinese pigs into commercial European lines.

pmc-12671070.title: Comparative genomics reveals diversity and taxonomic relationships among Clostridioides difficile phages
pmc-12671070.creator: Mohimenul Haque Rolin, Shakhinur Islam Mondal, Daniyal Karim, Nurnabi Azad Jewel, Tahsin Khan, Mustafizur Rahman, Arzuba Akter
pmc-12671070.description: Clostridioides difficile is associated with life-threatening antibiotic-associated diarrhea, colitis, and toxin-mediated infections. While antibiotics are the primary treatment against C. difficile infections, increasing resistance necessitates alternatives. Bacteriophages and bacteriophage-derived proteins, such as endolysins, hold promise as potential solutions. Understanding phage biology at the genomic level is crucial for their therapeutic use. We conducted a comparative genomic analysis of 44 C.

pmc-12675993.title: Evaluating the Financial Factors Influencing Maternal, Newborn, and Child Health in Africa: Tobit Regression and Data Envelopment Analysis
pmc-12675993.creator: Youssef Er-Rays, Meriem M'dioud, Hamid Ait-Lemqeddem, Badreddine El Moutaqi, Fuqing Wu
pmc-12675993.description: BackgroundDespite international efforts, maternal, newborn, and child health (MNCH) outcomes in Africa continue to lag due to inefficient health systems and underperforming financial frameworks. Financial factors—such as total health expenditure, health coverage indices, and spending per capita—are key but understudied drivers of MNCH service efficiency.

pmc-12686425.title: Hydrotime analysis and gene expression reveal that cytokinin mitigates the detrimental effects of salinity on seed vigor
pmc-12686425.creator: Sama Osali, Afshin Tavakoli, Negin Idelouei, Ali Ahmadi, Elias Soltani
pmc-12686425.description: This study investigated the impact of salinity stress and cytokinin application on quinoa (Chenopodium quinoa Willd.) seed quality, germination behavior, and gene expression. Four quinoa cultivars with differing salinity tolerance were evaluated under varying salinity levels (0, 25, 40 dS m⁻¹) and cytokinin treatment (0 and 0.75 µM 6-BA).

pmc-12836095.title: Serum proteome analysis detects early molecular signatures of disease progression in IgA nephropathy
pmc-12836095.creator: Tony Jialiang Chen, Eleni Skandalou, Katarina Fritz-Wallace, Terje Apeland, Thomas Knoop, Hans-Peter Marti, Øystein Eikrem, Jessica Furriol
pmc-12836095.description: BackgroundImmunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN) is a common cause of chronic kidney disease (CKD) and identifying early molecular signatures is crucial for IgAN risk stratification and timely intervention. In this study we used serum proteomics to investigate molecular differences between IgAN patients who progressed and those who remained stable before separation in kidney function became apparent.

pmc-13092456.title: Layered Double Hydroxide-Loaded Dl-3-n-Butylphthalide Alleviates Renal Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury by Regulating the PI3K-AKT-Nrf2 Signaling Pathway
pmc-13092456.creator: Yan Yan, Ke Wang, Li Ren, Jun-jie Ma, Xing-chun Zhu, Hao-feng Ding, Jia-xin Chu, Zhi-gao Zhu, Jing-yi Xia, Yi Xia, Yuan Xu, Meng-han He, Wen-rui Wang, Cong-li Zhang
pmc-13092456.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposeThis study aims to address the issues that limit the clinical application of Dl-3-n-butylphthalide (NBP) due to its poor water solubility and low bioavailability, and to explore its therapeutic potential in renal ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury. We attempted to utilize layered double hydroxide (LDH) to construct a novel nano-drug delivery system to enhance the stability and efficacy of NBP, and to deeply investigate its potential mechanism of action.MethodsBy loading NBP onto LDH, LDHs-NBP nanocomplexes were successfully constructed.

pmc-13154516.title: High INHBB expression in colorectal cancer is associated with poor prognosis and drives malignant phenotypes in tumor cells
pmc-13154516.creator: Huiyan Chen, Yao Wu, Zongxuan Huang, Di Luo, Ziming Wang, Junhong Wu, Tianyuan Zhou, Hu Zhao
pmc-13154516.description: BackgroundColorectal cancer (CRC) represents a prevalent global malignancy, with its progression intimately associated with biological processes such as oxidative stress and anoikis. This study aimed to evaluate a prognostic model derived from oxidative stress and anoikis-related genes (OARGs) in CRC and to elucidate the underlying mechanisms of the core gene, INHBB.

pmc-13474966.title: Clinical feasibility of chairside methylene blue-mediated photodynamic therapy for oral candidiasis
pmc-13474966.creator: Peiru Zhou, Furong Yang, Jiakun Fang, Jiangli Zheng, Yanhong Meng, Xu Zhang, Hong Hua
pmc-13474966.description: ObjectivesOral candidiasis is a common oral mucosal infection, and limitations of conventional antifungal therapy highlight the need for alternative chairside treatment approaches. This study aimed to assess the short-term clinical response, safety, and feasibility of a chairside methylene blue-mediated photodynamic therapy (MB-PDT) protocol for oral candidiasis, and to generate preliminary data to inform the design of future randomized controlled trials.

pmc-13507581.title: Long Noncoding RNA H19 Mediates STAT3‐Dependent Activation of Keratinocytes and Fibroblasts in Systemic Sclerosis Skin
pmc-13507581.creator: Begoña Caballero‐Ruiz, Christopher W. Wasson, Rebecca L. Ross, Francesco Del Galdo
pmc-13507581.description: ObjectiveDermal systemic sclerosis (SSc) fibroblasts and their exosomes can activate keratinocytes in SSc, with long noncoding RNA (lncRNA) H19 highlighted as the most up‐regulated RNA in their cargo compared with healthy controls (HCs). The role of H19 in SSc pathogenesis has never been investigated.
